platforms.title: Instagram
platforms.summary: You cannot fully disable recommendations, but you can switch to Following, reset suggested content, and cut notification pull. Use Open links to jump into Instagram or Accounts Center — some screens only finish inside the mobile app.

controls.title: Use the Following feed
controls.body: Open Instagram → tap For you at the top → select Following. This shows posts from people you follow in a more chronological order instead of the algorithmic For You mix.

controls.title: Reset suggested content
controls.body: Profile → ☰ → Content preferences → Reset suggested content. This clears signals used for Reels, Explore, and suggested posts without unfollowing anyone.

controls.title: Mark posts Not interested
controls.body: On any suggested post or Reel, tap ⋯ → Not interested (or Hide). Repeat on topics that waste your time so the algorithm gets fewer wrong signals.

controls.title: Turn off non-DM notifications
controls.body: Profile → ☰ → Notifications. Disable likes, comments, follower alerts, and live videos. Keep message alerts only if you need them for real conversations.

controls.title: Set a daily time reminder
controls.body: Profile → Your activity → Time management → set a reminder below your current average. This screen is app-only on most devices — open Instagram, then follow the guide if the menu looks different.

platforms.title: TikTok
platforms.summary: TikTok lets you turn off personalized feeds and refresh the For You page — one of the stronger built-in controls. Links open TikTok; finish Screen Time and Content preferences inside the app.

controls.title: Turn off Personalized feeds
controls.body: Profile → ☰ → Settings and privacy → Content preferences → turn Personalized feeds Off. Bonus: also turn Personalized search Off.

controls.title: Refresh your For You feed
controls.body: Settings and privacy → Content preferences → Refresh your For You feed. Use this when the feed feels junked up, then be selective about what you watch next.

controls.title: Prefer the Following tab
controls.body: Open the Following tab instead of For You when you only want updates from people you chose to follow.

controls.title: Enable Screen Time limits and breaks
controls.body: Settings and privacy → Screen time → set a daily limit (start at 30–45 minutes) and turn on Screen Time Breaks every 10–30 minutes.

controls.title: Mute engagement notifications
controls.body: Settings and privacy → Notifications → turn off Likes, Comments, and New followers so the app stops pulling you back mid-focus.

platforms.title: YouTube
platforms.summary: Home is always algorithmic. Use Subscriptions, kill autoplay, and manage watch/search history to weaken personalized recommendations.

controls.title: Open Subscriptions instead of Home
controls.body: On mobile, tap Subscriptions in the bottom bar. On desktop, open Subscriptions from the left menu and bookmark it. This shows channels you chose, in chronological order.

controls.title: Turn off Autoplay
controls.body: While watching a video, turn Autoplay off at the bottom of the player. Also check Settings → Playback and performance / General → Autoplay next video.

controls.title: Pause or clear watch & search history
controls.body: Open YouTube History or Google My Activity. Delete recent history, set auto-delete (e.g. 3 months), or pause watch/search history so new watches stop training recommendations.

controls.title: Use Not interested / Don’t recommend channel
controls.body: On any Home recommendation, tap ⋯ → Not interested or Don’t recommend channel. This is the fastest way to prune junk without deleting your account.

controls.title: Avoid or time-limit Shorts
controls.body: Skip the Shorts tab. If you use Shorts, set a separate 15-minute phone limit. Shorts use the same variable-reward loop as TikTok.

controls.title: Set Take a Break and bedtime reminders
controls.body: Profile → Settings → General / Time watched → Reminders. Set a break every 30–60 minutes and a bedtime reminder so evening sessions have an exit ramp.

platforms.title: X / Twitter
platforms.summary: Switch to Following for a chronological feed, then prune interests and topics the platform thinks you care about.

controls.title: Switch to Following
controls.body: At the top of Home, tap Following instead of For you. This is the main way to escape the algorithmic mix — you may need to reselect it each session.

controls.title: Remove inferred interests
controls.body: Settings and privacy → Privacy and safety → Content you see → Interests. Uncheck topics you do not want shaping your feed.

controls.title: Trim ads preferences
controls.body: Privacy and safety → Ads preferences. Uncheck options you do not want used for targeting. Also mute or block ads you repeatedly dislike.

controls.title: Mute and unfollow high-scroll accounts
controls.body: Mute keywords, phrases, and accounts that trigger endless threads. Unfollow accounts you open only out of habit.

platforms.title: Facebook
platforms.summary: The main Home feed stays personalized. Use Feeds for a chronological friends/pages view and Quiet Mode for scheduled focus.

controls.title: Open the Feeds view
controls.body: Menu → Feeds (near the bottom of the menu). This shows recent posts from friends and pages you follow with far less algorithmic junk. Bookmark it on desktop if you can.

controls.title: Use Favorites for people you actually care about
controls.body: Menu → Feeds → Favorites (or Home feed preferences). Pin close friends and important pages so they surface without the full Home algorithm.

controls.title: Snooze or Unfollow noisy sources
controls.body: On any post → ⋯ → Snooze for 30 days or Unfollow. This cleans the feed without ending friendships.

controls.title: Schedule Quiet Mode
controls.body: Menu → Settings → Quiet Mode (or Digital Wellbeing tools). Mute notifications during study/work blocks and evenings.

platforms.title: Reddit
platforms.summary: Turn off Home feed recommendations and stick to subscriptions you chose on purpose.

controls.title: Disable Home feed recommendations
controls.body: Avatar → Settings → Account settings → turn off Enable home feed recommendations (wording may vary slightly by app version). Your Home should lean toward subscribed communities.

controls.title: Sort by New or Top — not Best
controls.body: In each subreddit, change the sort from Best/Hot to New or Top (day/week). This reduces engagement-optimized ranking.

controls.title: Unsubscribe from doomscroll subs
controls.body: Leave communities that reliably pull you into multi-hour rabbit holes. Keep learning, hobby, and utility subs only.

controls.title: Cut Reddit push notifications
controls.body: Settings → Notifications. Disable inbox pings you do not need. Use email digests only if useful.

platforms.title: LinkedIn
platforms.summary: LinkedIn is one of the few platforms that makes chronological feeds both temporary and permanent.

controls.title: Switch to Most recent (session)
controls.body: Above the feed, open Select feed view → Most recent first. Use this when you only want updates from your network.

controls.title: Make Most recent your default
controls.body: Me → Settings & Privacy → Feed preferences → Most recent posts. LinkedIn is unusually good at letting this stick.

controls.title: Unfollow viral noise without disconnecting
controls.body: On posts that waste time → ⋯ → Unfollow or Mute. You stay connected but stop seeing their engagement bait.

platforms.title: Snapchat
platforms.summary: Personalized Discover can be limited in some regions; streaks and Stories still create strong daily pull. Many controls are app-only — links open Snapchat or Accounts.

controls.title: Disable personalized content (where available)
controls.body: Profile → Settings → Advanced services / European Union Controls → turn off Show personalized content if the option appears in your region.

controls.title: Let low-value streaks expire
controls.body: Streaks create daily obligation, not connection. Let streaks with distant contacts expire and keep only people you actually talk to.

controls.title: Limit Snapchat notifications
controls.body: Phone Settings → Notifications → Snapchat: keep only direct chats if needed. Disable Stories and Discover alerts. Or adjust alerts inside Snapchat settings.

platforms.title: Pinterest
platforms.summary: There is no full algorithm off-switch. You can only tune the home feed and reduce autoplay / shopping signals.

controls.title: Tune your home feed
controls.body: Settings → Home feed tuner / Tune your home feed. Turn off sources and topics that keep recommending junk.

controls.title: Limit data used for recommendations
controls.body: Settings → Privacy & data. Reduce ad personalization and related targeting where available.

controls.title: Turn off automatic video playback
controls.body: Settings → Social permissions / Video. Disable autoplay so boards stop becoming infinite video feeds.
